step4.objective:
• Multicast traffic for a source-specific group is forwarded only to interfaces with an active IGMPv3 join for that (S,G) pair once the join is processed.
  • The multicast routing table reflects an accurate (S,G) entry, including incoming interface, outgoing interface list, and forwarding state, immediately after a host joins the group.
  • A statically configured mroute at the last-hop router is honored, with the source and receiver interfaces correctly reflected in the routing table alongside dynamically learned PIM-SSM entries.
  • Multicast traffic is not forwarded to interfaces or hosts that have not issued a valid source-specific join for the group.
  • Joins for groups or sources outside the configured SSM range are rejected or handled per SSM policy, with no erroneous forwarding state created.
  • The CLI command to display the PIM multicast routing table is accepted and returns output consistent with the actual PIM-SSM/static mroute forwarding state.
  • Multicast forwarding and routing table state remain correct and consistent across combinations of dynamically joined and statically configured mroute entries.
  • Routing table entries are updated or removed appropriately when group membership or source reachability changes, preventing stale or orphaned forwarding state.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Set up SSM topology: multicast source, last-hop router (LHR) with PIM-SSM enabled, and a receiver host capable of IGMPv3, with the SSM range configured on the LHR.
Configure a static mroute at the LHR for a known (S,G) pair, specifying source and receiver interfaces.
Verify the CLI command to display the PIM multicast routing table is accepted and returns baseline output before any dynamic join.
Test with the receiver host issuing a valid IGMPv3 source-specific join for an (S,G) pair within the configured SSM range.
Verify the PIM mroute table reflects an accurate (S,G) entry immediately after the join, including correct incoming interface, outgoing interface list, and forwarding state.
Send multicast traffic from the source for the joined (S,G) and confirm it is forwarded only to the interface with the active join.
Confirm interfaces/hosts that have not issued a join for the (S,G) do not receive the multicast traffic.
Verify the statically configured mroute entry and the dynamically learned PIM-SSM entry both appear correctly in the routing table, with source and receiver interfaces accurately reflected for each.
Test with a join request for a group or source outside the configured SSM range and verify it is rejected or handled per SSM policy.
Verify no erroneous forwarding state or mroute entry is created as a result of the out-of-range join attempt.
Set the receiver host to leave the group (or expire membership) and verify the corresponding mroute entry is updated or removed from the routing table.
Test with the multicast source becoming unreachable and verify stale or orphaned forwarding state for the affected (S,G) is not retained.
Verify the PIM mroute table remains consistent and accurate when re-querying via the CLI across combinations of remaining static and dynamic entries.
